text: {"observations":"Harmonic stacks extending to about 6 kHz show wavy vibrato (clearest around 2.5-4.3 s) and continuous pitch glides between notes (e.g. near 4.1 s and 5 s). This points to a bowed string and rules out piano (fixed pitches, decaying notes) and flute (far fewer harmonics). The harmonics are closely spaced, roughly 150-250 Hz apart, and the strongest energy lies below about 800 Hz, reaching down towards 100-200 Hz. That suggests low fundamentals in the cello range rather than a violin, though this is a judgement from spacing estimates and not certain.","answer":"C"}
